notes: Zeek conn.log appears in public security datasets, so the format is probably not unseen. What makes it a held-out source is the VOCABULARY: originator and responder are not source and destination, and half the columns describe things ECS 8.11 has no field for. HAZARD: four column names contain a dot. A csv extraction declaring `id.orig_h` produces a Logstash field whose name literally contains a dot, which is legal and is not nesting.

fields.note: Identifies the CONNECTION, which spans many events and many Zeek logs. event.id identifies an event, so it is not the same thing, and ECS 8.11 offers nothing for a cross-log correlation handle.
`orig` is the handshake initiator, which is what ECS calls the source. Nothing in the name says src.
tcp/udp/icmp is the TRANSPORT. The pair with `service` is the trap: one is network.transport and the other is network.protocol.
dns/http is the APPLICATION protocol, which ECS calls network.protocol. Unset as `-` on connections Zeek could not classify.
SECONDS as a decimal. ECS event.duration is NANOSECONDS as a long and the IR carries no unit conversion, so assigning it is wrong by nine orders of magnitude.
S0, SF, RSTO, REJ. A Zeek-internal summary of how the connection ended. It is not event.outcome: a connection that was reset is not a failed security event, and SF does not mean success.
Whether the originator falls inside Zeek's configured local networks. A property of the sensor's configuration, not of the event.
The mirror of local_orig: whether the responder falls inside Zeek's configured local networks. A property of the sensor's configuration.
Bytes the sensor failed to capture. Describes the observer's fidelity, not the traffic. ECS 8.11 has no field for it.
One letter per connection event, in order. A Zeek-specific encoding.

Total IP-layer bytes including headers. source.bytes is already taken by orig_bytes, which is the payload count, and ECS offers no second byte counter per direction. Only one of the two can be source.bytes.
The mirror of orig_ip_bytes: total IP-layer bytes including headers. destination.bytes is already taken by resp_bytes, the payload count.
A set of connection identifiers, not a value.

origin: Produced by running the software, not copied from documentation or a public dataset. Captured on 2 October 2026 on the project's own Docker host.
